risks.text: A new type-error variant must be added in two crates: its message in baml_compiler2_hir_ty/src/diagnostics.rs and its DiagnosticId/rendering in baml_db/src/check.rs; missing one of them loses or mislabels the diagnostic (history 3caf4c1, 2143382 - diagnostics.rs:289,1404; check.rs:2040,2149).

Inference that reads a still-unsolved inference variable silently finalizes it as Error with no diagnostic, and the program miscompiles or panics later at emission; generics and operator receivers must be resolved before member lookup (history 3caf4c1 - infer.rs:8808-8822).

Operator checks deliberately skip Error and inference-variable operands to avoid cascading errors, but not `unknown`; changing that filter changes which errors users see (history 9dbb5f4 for `?.` on nullable scrutinees - infer.rs:5698-5706).

The deferred_operator_receiver.baml fixture is the regression test for the generic-operator-receiver panic ("indirect calls require an explicit caller layout"); deleting or weakening it removes the only guard (history 3caf4c1 - deferred_operator_receiver.baml:1-5).

Rust tests that call baml_db setup_test_db re-derive the whole stdlib in every nextest process; use the baml_test_support prefixed helpers, which splice in the stdlib compiled at build time (TEST_INSTRUCTIONS.md "Rust tests: import the prefixed compile helpers").

risks.text: Each BexThread has a 10 MiB stack budget counting frames and slots; going past it fails the VM thread, so deep-recursion changes and tests must stay under it (history 3039309 - bex_vm/src/vm/frame_stack.rs:19, re-exported vm.rs:183).

Registering a root call must reject an already-cancelled call under the same lock that call-ID cancellation takes; cleanup bodies deliberately skip that check. Moving either check out of the lock brings back the all_settled cancellation race (history 166bbc0 - the reject_cancelled check at bex_engine/src/lib.rs:617, after the active_calls lock taken at :591-612).

Bad Boundary telemetry settings (level, empty key, bad URL) must become an InvalidConfiguration diagnostic that disables recording with a warning; returning an error instead makes SDK load fail for the user (history 0c11e94 - bex_engine/src/telemetry.rs:174,285-321,637).

Native HTTP clients are cached per (connect timeout, proxy and CA environment variables), at most 32, cleared on overflow; a new environment input reqwest reads must be added to HTTP_CLIENT_ENV or the cached client goes stale (history 4da8e1d - sys_native/src/io_impls.rs:2962,3007).

Subprocess kill goes through a per-process kill channel and the child is spawned with kill_on_drop(false), so dropping a handle does not kill the child; the baml wrapper depends on this API (history 591d6d1 - io_impls.rs:1374,1467,1894).

groups.title: btel_* crates: recording, snapshots and delivery of BAML telemetry to the cloud (BCS), plus baml query over it

checks.run: cd baml_language && cargo nextest run -p btel_bcs
checks.why: delivery config and plan tests (delivery.rs tests)
workspace lints with -D warnings (mise.toml)

risks.text: Shutdown delivery is bounded: after shutdown_timeout (5s) pending data is dropped with ShutdownTimeout, and the worker runtime is not dropped while a DNS lookup hangs; unbounding it lets an unreachable endpoint hold the user process open (history a09a719 - btel_bcs/src/delivery.rs:116-145,1099-1105).

The delivery reqwest client is built without explicit proxy settings so it follows the environment proxy (HTTPS_PROXY etc.); adding no_proxy() or a custom transport breaks users behind a proxy (history f6b65b3 - delivery.rs:1097).

Sensitive request headers such as proxy-authorization are scrubbed in the delivery plan; a new header carrying credentials must be added to that list or it leaks into recordings (btel_bcs/src/plan.rs:129).

checks.why: Rust SDK generator unit tests, including alias-cycle boxing (sdkgen_rust/src/lib.rs:816)

risks.text: The Rust SDK box-cycle analysis counts type aliases as containment edges; a class that reaches itself through an alias needs a Box or the generated code does not compile (history 83c3abe - sdkgen_rust/src/analyze.rs:362-366, tests lib.rs:816,892; emit/type_alias.rs).

baml.json.json maps to serde_json::Value and is special-cased in analyze.rs (has_serde) and translate_ty.rs; the two must agree or json fields lose serde derives or are skipped again (history 51fb016 - analyze.rs:561, translate_ty.rs:81,277).

The C# host requires the bridge function table at exactly ABI revision 5; changing the table without bumping the revision in every SDK makes hosts load a mismatched bridge (sdks/csharp/ABI.md:12,222).

risks.text: Nightly releases run build-baml-wrapper as a no-op and the fingerprint check is invoked with --allow_missing baml-wrapper-candidates; canary still requires them, so a new workflow condition or artifact family has to be changed in both the workflow and release-fingerprints (history a2ff141 - `enabled` at release-baml-language.yml:423 and --allow_missing at :655; main.baml:241,290 accepts only one missing family name).

Every artifact family a release uploads needs a Family entry (Fingerprinted or Unfingerprinted with a reason) and a place in the expected list at the bottom of main.baml, or the fingerprint check fails the release (history 857c3f2 - tools/release-fingerprints/baml_src/main.baml:88-102,320-335).

Build images must come through the GCP ghcr-cache prefix; replacing literal ghcr.io in workflow YAML misses the maturin and cross-rs 0.2.5 implicit defaults, and the CROSS_CONFIG of the toolchain and wrapper jobs overrides Cross.toml (docs/ci-infra-gcp.md; the image = lines at baml_language/Cross.toml:18,24; release/platforms.json).

cross forwards only the environment variables listed in Cross.toml passthrough (BAML_GIT_SHA, RUSTFLAGS, CFLAGS, CXXFLAGS); a new variable the build needs, such as the source fingerprint, never reaches the compiler inside the container unless listed (baml_language/Cross.toml:21,27 passthrough lines).

docs/ci-infra-gcp.md describes a manually provisioned cache repository (no IaC); its administrative gcloud commands are provisioning history, not CI steps, and must not be run to "refresh" a working repository (docs/ci-infra-gcp.md "Administrative setup").

checks.run: cd baml_language && cargo nextest run -p baml_tests

rules.rule: BAML files under baml_builtins2/baml_std stay formatted by baml fmt.
rules.why: The pre-commit baml-fmt-stdlib hook rejects the commit and unformatted stdlib diverges for everyone.

rules.rule: Crates built for wasm do not use std::time::SystemTime or Instant.
rules.why: Those calls panic or fail to build on wasm32, breaking the web and playground SDKs; clippy-wasm enforces it.

rules.rule: Runtime code reads the environment through baml_env::os_var; clippy rejects std::env::var, var_os, vars and vars_os via disallowed-methods.
rules.why: Env access is centralized in baml_env (the HTTP client cache key is built from it), so a direct read bypasses that and fails mise run clippy.

rules.rule: A telemetry configuration or delivery problem warns and disables recording; it never fails startup or blocks shutdown beyond the bounded timeout.
rules.why: SDK load or process exit would break for users with a bad level, key, URL or unreachable endpoint.

rules.rule: Changing the bridge function table bumps the ABI revision in every SDK host.
rules.why: Hosts require the exact revision and refuse to load a mismatched bridge.

rules.rule: Every artifact family a release uploads has a Family entry in release-fingerprints main.baml and carries the source fingerprint.
rules.why: The fingerprint check in release-baml-language.yml fails the whole release.

rules.rule: Release build images are pulled through the us-central1 ghcr-cache prefix, using upstream tags.
rules.why: Direct ghcr.io pulls bring back GHCR rate and availability failures in release CI.

rules.rule: The TextMate grammar and language configuration are edited only in typescript2/pkg-grammar and synced to the VS Code extension.
rules.why: The pre-commit grammar-single-source check fails and the editor copies drift.
